issues.legal_issue: A conviction may rest on the cumulative effect of the evidence even when some eyewitness accounts are unreliable and another witness is not wholly reliable, provided the evidence as a whole establishes guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
material_facts: The prosecution case arose from prior hostility between the accused and the deceased’s side over a field, including an earlier incident on the day of the killing.
Several proposed eyewitnesses were disbelieved or treated as unreliable because of inconsistencies, unexplained presence, or other credibility concerns.
A local witness whose testimony was not wholly reliable described the assault, and the court considered the evidence of other local witnesses sufficient to corroborate it.
The medical evidence recorded numerous injuries consistent with a severe beating.
The trial court and the High Court found the charges proved beyond reasonable doubt.
issues.conclusion: The cumulative evidence was sufficiently convincing to sustain the convictions for rioting and murder with common object.
issues.legal_principle: A witness’s relationship to a victim does not, by itself, justify rejecting the witness’s testimony; reliability must be assessed on the facts of the particular case (Dalip Singh v. State of Punjab). A partially reliable witness may provide a basis for conviction when sufficiently corroborated (Vadivelu Thevar v. State of Madras). Chance-witness testimony is not necessarily false but may be unsafe to rely on without careful assessment. The court applied these principles to convictions under Sections 147 and 302 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The accused challenged criminal convictions on appeal.
predicates.eyewitness_accounts_converged_on_the_ass: Prosecution witnesses gave accounts supporting that the accused assaulted the victim, although the reliability of individual accounts varied.
predicates.partly_reliable_testimony_was_corroborat: Testimony assessed as only partly reliable was supported by other witnesses whose evidence the court accepted.
predicates.prior_hostility_supported_the_prosecutio: The parties had a prior dispute and tension that supported the prosecution account of the occurrence.
predicates.medical_injuries_were_consistent_with_th: Medical evidence recorded injuries consistent with the alleged severe assault.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a conviction and the eyewitness evidence converges on the assault, partly reliable testimony is corroborated, and the surrounding hostility and medical evidence support the account, the conviction is sustainable.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court should not interfere under Article 136 with concurrent factual findings of guilt when consideration of the evidence as a whole does not show those findings to be erroneous.
material_facts: The trial court convicted the accused, and the High Court upheld the convictions and sentences.
The Supreme Court considered the evidence as a whole, including its weaknesses and corroborating circumstances, and did not find the concurrent findings of guilt to be erroneous.
The accused did not substantiate their pleas of alibi.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere under Article 136, upheld the convictions and sentences, and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 136 of the Constitution, the Court assessed whether the concurrent findings of fact were really erroneous and whether the case warranted appellate interference; disagreement with the assessment of individual witnesses did not, on the totality of the evidence, make this a fit case for intervention.

predicates.criminal_special_leave_appeal_from_convi: The accused brought a special-leave appeal challenging criminal convictions.
predicates.trial_and_appellate_courts_made_concurre: The trial court and the appellate court both found the accused guilty on the evidence.
predicates.totality_of_evidence_did_not_show_those_: On considering the evidence as a whole, the Supreme Court did not find the concurrent findings of guilt to be erroneous.

issues.definition: In a special-leave appeal from a conviction, when the trial and appellate courts made concurrent factual findings that are not shown erroneous by the evidence as a whole, appellate interference is unwarranted.
